page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-24 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, the system provides 24 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features an extensive cache hierarchy, including 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic hardware acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 186.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage disks or integrated hardware GPUs, requiring persistent data to be attached via networked block storage. In terms of data throughput, memory subsystem benchmarks demonstrate an uncached read bandwidth of 139.8 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 57.72 GB/sec for large 256 MB blocks, scaling up to 1671.9 GB/sec for cached 16 KB blocks.

Benchmark results place general compute and memory capabilities largely within median industry thresholds, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1913.0 and a multi-core score of 13540.0. The instance registers stronger relative performance in Geekbench image processing (13623.0) and text processing (2480.0), both ranking in the top quartile. In machine learning workloads, AMX capabilities assist in achieving top-decile text generation throughput on small 135M language models at 394.04 tokens per second, though medium 7B model generation settles into median performance at 15.34 tokens per second.

With its generous memory allocation relative to core count and specialized matrix math instructions, the c4-highmem-24 offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-bound applications without the financial overhead of dedicated GPU accelerators. The primary operational tradeoff stems from the absence of local NVMe storage. This instance is technically suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, medium-scale ETL pipelines, and lightweight CPU-based matrix and AI inference tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-24 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual instance equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs on 12 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 186.0 GB of system memory. Its processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and Intel AMX matrix extensions. The configuration lacks integrated GPU hardware and bundled local storage, requiring network-attached disks for persistence. Standard benchmarks indicate average tier general compute and memory throughput, complemented by strong results in image processing, text processing, and CPU-driven small model language generation. The 7.75 GB per vCPU ratio makes it cost-efficient for memory-dense services that do not require high-IOPS local scratch disks, making it suitable for in-memory caching systems, data processing pipelines, and enterprise backend workloads.
